topics.topic: Revocation visibility for requests already in flight at commit
questions: What must happen when a request authenticates before revocation commits but performs a later authorization check or protected write after the commit?
Is the in-flight revocation case intentionally accepted as permitted behavior, or must it remain unresolved until A11 defines it?
Must a request authenticated before the revocation commit but reaching its project-scope or capability check afterward observe the revocation?
Must a request authenticated before the revocation commit but reaching its project-access check after the commit observe the revocation?

quotes: None; the next guard check sees the revocation.
judgement.why: State 5 explicitly requires the next project guard check to observe a committed grant or assignment revocation, including when authentication occurred earlier.

topics.topic: Temporal validity and refusal rules for supplied ServiceCredential.expires_at
questions: Which temporal values of a caller-supplied ServiceCredential.expires_at must credential issuance refuse?
May a credential be issued with `expires_at <= now`, or must issuance reject an expiry that is not in the future?
May a newly issued service credential have `expires_at` equal to or earlier than the operation time, or must a non-null expiry be strictly in the future?

quotes:
The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the principal id
and an optional `expires_at`. Any expiry is accepted and stored as
supplied, a past one included, never converted (A28 keeps a supplied time); no expiry means the credential does not expire. A
credential is usable only before its expiry, so one issued with an expiry
already reached is stored but never authenticates.
judgement.why: State 5 explicitly accepts every supplied expiry, including one at or before issuance time, while making an already-expired credential unusable.

topics.topic: Timezone representation and normalization of supplied ServiceCredential.expires_at
questions: How is a source-supplied offset-aware expires_at handled before persistence?
What happens when the issuing request supplies an offset-aware or non-UTC `expires_at`?
Which supplied timestamp forms are accepted for `ServiceCredential.expires_at`, and must an offset-aware value be rejected or converted to an equivalent UTC offset-naive value?

quotes:
The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the principal id
and an optional `expires_at`. Any expiry is accepted and stored as
supplied, a past one included, never converted (A28 keeps a supplied time); no expiry means the credential does not expire. A
credential is usable only before its expiry, so one issued with an expiry
already reached is stored but never authenticates.
judgement.why: State 5 says any supplied expiry is accepted, stored as supplied, and never converted, thereby excluding normalization to UTC-naive form.

topics.topic: Whether an archived-project progress read may create and persist a manual budget version
questions: Does the named progress-read exception override A4/A5's archived-mutation refusal, and at what point in the guard is that exception applied?
Does this read bypass the archived-mutation guard and commit the budget version, or must archived reads remain free of this write?
Does the named progress-read side effect override A5 and PLAT-REG-003 for an archived project, or must the read return without creating the manual budget version?

quotes:
An archived Registry project is readable and refuses every mutation of its
budget, snapshot import and activation, expense, document, progress, payment
and photo records (accepted `rules.registry_status_policy`: archived reads,
never mutates), with one named exception: a staff read of a project's
progress list, when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates
that empty manual budget version, also for an archived project (Factory code
`domain/project_tracking.py` 50–60, `api/router.py` 434–438); no other
operation changes the budget of an archived project.
judgement.divergence: The exception commits an empty manual BudgetVersion during the archived-project progress read, whereas A5 rejects the same hidden mutation; authorized staff and later budget readers observe whether the version exists.
judgement.why: R0-24 expressly permits this one archived-project write, while A5's unqualified archived-state row rejects every portal mutation.

witness.initial: Registry reports project P as archived, P has no manual BudgetVersion, and an assigned active staff member may read it.
events: The staff member requests P's progress list.
The project guard receives the archived Registry status.
The progress-list operation attempts to ensure the manual budget exists.
outcomes: The read succeeds and persists an empty manual BudgetVersion under the named R0-24 exception.
The attempted creation is rejected as `archived_project` under A5.
witness.observer: The requesting staff member and later staff inspecting P's budget-version history.
basis:

and photo records (accepted `rules.registry_status_policy`: archived reads,
never mutates), with one named exception: a staff read of a project's
progress list, when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates
that empty manual budget version, also for an archived project (Factory code
`domain/project_tracking.py` 50–60, `api/router.py` 434–438); no other
operation changes the budget of an archived project.

An existing grant or assignment is not new access: it keeps giving read
access, also after the viewer receives a new access link or the staff
account is reinstated, because neither operation consults the Registry
(accepted notes `issue_viewer_access`, `change_staff_status`).

topics.topic: Initial status and activation metadata of the implicitly created manual BudgetVersion
questions: What status and activation metadata does the implicitly created empty manual BudgetVersion receive?

quotes:
A18: at most one manual version per project; a new one is `inactive` and is
never activated implicitly; A13 (`budget.manual_version_create` only when it
is created).
judgement.why: State 5 makes the implicitly created manual version inactive and forbids implicit activation, so activation metadata is not populated by this creation.

topics.topic: Required outcome of concurrent progress reads racing to create the manual budget version
questions: When concurrent progress reads both observe no manual version, must both reads succeed by converging on one version, or may one fail after the uniqueness race?

quotes:
A18: at most one manual version per project; a new one is `inactive` and is
never activated implicitly; A13 (`budget.manual_version_create` only when it
is created).
judgement.why: State 5 enforces uniqueness through persistence and permits a racing request to fail because the resulting persistence failure propagates rather than being retried or converted into success.

topics.topic: Whether ServiceCredential.expires_at is request-supplied or derived from a TTL
questions: Is `ServiceCredential.expires_at` preserved from the issuing request, or must it be derived from the operation clock and a TTL—and, if derived, which TTL?

quotes:
The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the principal id
and an optional `expires_at`. Any expiry is accepted and stored as
supplied, a past one included, never converted (A28 keeps a supplied time); no expiry means the credential does not expire. A
credential is usable only before its expiry, so one issued with an expiry
already reached is stored but never authenticates.
judgement.why: State 5 explicitly preserves the request-supplied optional expiry and defines no service-credential TTL derivation.

topics.topic: Whether audit occurred_at may differ from the operation's other timestamps
questions: Must an operation’s audit `occurred_at` equal its other timestamps, or may the audit writer’s later clock read differ?

quotes:
The one exception is the audit record's `occurred_at`: the audit
writer takes it when it appends (Factory code `application/audit_writer.py`
136).

A test per multi-write operation (activation, revocation cascades,
bootstrap) that its written timestamps are one instant.
judgement.divergence: The normative exception permits an audit appended later to have a different `occurred_at`, while the required bootstrap test demands one instant for all timestamps; auditors and test runners observe the difference.
judgement.why: The required test does not exclude audit timestamps even though the normative rule expressly exempts `AuditRecord.occurred_at` from the operation's captured instant.

witness.initial: The staff table is empty and the clock advances between creation of the first administrator and append of its audit record.
events: The bootstrap operation creates the administrator with `created_at` equal to T.
The audit writer appends `staff.create` at T plus one millisecond.
The required bootstrap timestamp test compares the written records.
outcomes: Bootstrap succeeds with different account and audit timestamps because `occurred_at` is expressly taken at append.
The implementation or test requires both timestamps to equal one instant.
witness.observer: The bootstrap test runner and an auditor reading the account and audit records.
basis:
The local command creates the single first staff account
on an empty staff table: role administrator, status active, email verified,
no creator; its audit is `staff.create` by the system actor with the created
`staff_id`, result success.

The emptiness check and both inserts run in one
write transaction that no concurrent attempt can interleave, so concurrent attempts create exactly one
account; when any staff account exists the command refuses with
`BootstrapAlreadyCompleted` and nothing persists.
